hero.title: File:Riga 1612 panorama by Heinrich Thum.jpg
hero.artist: Heinrich Thum; Nicolaus Mollin Typography (Printed by Nikolaus Mollyn). "Mollyn was able to prepare books in two-color printing (red and black). He used not only high-quality paper, but also printed on parchment. The activities of the first known Riga bookbinders are associated with Mollyns' printing house. The first and for a long time the only bookstore in Riga operated at Mollyns' printing house on Krāmu Street. Mollyn printed images in woodcut, copper engraving, etching techniques and thus established the beginnings of book graphics and printed graphics as an art genre in Riga. In 1602, the first Riga copper engraver, Heinrich Thum, began working at Mollyn's printing house. The Riga panoramas (1589, 1625) and the surrounding area plan (1622) printed in Mollyn' printing house are the first city views drawn in Riga on the spot (in situ) and published there. Mollyn provided and commissioned a unique large-scale copper engraving – the Riga Panorama of 1612, and the first Riga bookplates were also printed (1602, 1605)."
hero.description: Panorama of the city of Riga in 1612.

gallery.credit: This digital media file - and/or the physical objects depicted on it - originates from the digital and/or physical collections of the Koninklijke Bibliotheek, national library of the Netherlands.
gallery.description: This map depicts the Baltic states Latvia and Estonia. Ever since the Treaty of Altmar in 1629 this area was a Swedish province which was mainly inhabited by Germans. The map was published in 1662 in the second volume of Joan Blaeus Atlas Maior. As a basis for this map, Blaeu used a large-size wall map from the Swedish scientist Anders Bureus (1571-1661), who was head of the topographical survey.
